_README: Mission environments and their one-way signal delay to Earth. one_way_delay_s is the value used by the Earth-independent mode rule; for Mars it is the worst case (conjunction-side maximum). delay_range_s documents the real range when it varies.

station.name: Low Earth orbit
station.source: Prototype approximation: near real-time voice and data via NASA's relay satellites (light time from low Earth orbit is far below 1 s).

lunar_base.name: Lunar base
lunar_base.source: Light travel time over the mean Earth-Moon distance (384,400 km / speed of light ≈ 1.3 s). NASA, Challenges in Communications for Exploration Class Missions: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20250002660

mars_transit.name: Mars transit
mars_transit.source: One-way delay between Earth and Mars varies from about 3 to 22 minutes with planetary positions; the worst case (22 min) is used. NASA, Challenges in Communications for Exploration Class Missions: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20250002660

autonomy._README: PROTOTYPE DESIGN CHOICES, NOT NASA RULES. Earth-independent mode is active when the overall level is critical AND the round trip (2 x one_way_delay_s) exceeds round_trip_threshold_s. ground_response_s is an assumed time for the flight surgeon to read and answer a report; it is only used to estimate earliest_reply_s and the countdown, never in the rule itself.
